value.rationale: The actual gap is the paired asymptotic law of two naturally different invariantly sampled views of the SAME classical oscillator: uniformly distributed log extinction shares under physical-time sampling versus linear abundance shares under a canonically normalized reaction-flux bias, with every fixed positive mixed moment evaluated by Beta(r,s). This explains a significant scale separation obscured by exact first-moment and period formulas; these distributions and all higher mixed moments do not follow mechanically from the previously known covariance identity. Natural physical and flux measures, quantitative W1 rate, and exact universal coefficients make the result useful despite the classical model and modest proof length.
